facts.statement: One base player body diameter is the spatial normalization unit.
facts.method: Defines the project unit and anchors all footage normalization.

facts.statement: Base maximum health is normalized to one.
facts.method: Defines the health unit used by proportional card and damage values.

facts.statement: The damage and environment collider is approximately circular, while arms, gun, face, and hat are presentation.

tolerance.value: stable rolling contact and radial hits

facts.method: Compared rotating body silhouettes, ledge contacts, and projectile impacts.

facts.statement: Base sustained horizontal speed is about 0.11 player diameters per simulation tick.
facts.method: Normalized unobstructed and airborne horizontal trajectories against 17-19 pixel body diameters in two recordings.

facts.statement: Ground control reaches sustained speed in roughly eight ticks.
facts.method: Estimated the short velocity ramp after direction changes visible at 30 fps.

facts.statement: Airborne horizontal control retains most ground authority.
facts.method: Compared long airborne lateral corrections with ground starts.

facts.statement: A player stores one jump that may be used on the ground or in the air and is restored by ground contact.
facts.method: Cross-checked the moveset description with ledge-fall and grounded-jump sequences.

facts.statement: A base jump begins near 0.21 player diameters per tick upward.
facts.method: Fit a ballistic arc to unmodified-looking jumps after normalizing player diameter.

facts.statement: Base airborne gravity is near 0.009 player diameters per tick squared.
facts.method: Derived gravity from measured jump height and time-to-apex ranges.

facts.statement: A base jump rises roughly 2.5 player diameters above takeoff.
facts.method: Compared takeoff and apex body centers against the measured player diameter.

facts.statement: A base jump reaches its apex in about 23 ticks.
facts.method: Counted 30 fps frames from takeoff to apex and converted each frame to two simulation ticks.

facts.statement: Releasing horizontal input damps ground velocity quickly without an immediate hard stop.
facts.method: Estimated deceleration from short settling motions on flat platforms.

facts.statement: The circular body rotates visibly from contacts, recoil, and knockback while aim remains world-directed.

tolerance.value: body rotation does not rotate aim input

facts.method: Observed independent body roll and gun aiming in both recordings.

facts.statement: Base players do not regenerate health during a duel.
facts.method: Observed persistent damage between hits where no healing card was present.
